articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! One Piece is going to make history with the upcoming God Valley film. This year’s One Piece Day was a major surprise to fans when the anime confirmed two upcoming films of the series. While the first film is scheduled to be released next year, the other film will premiere in 2029. While all this is going on, the anime is also continuing its yearly schedule ever since the Elbaph Arc began. The manga commenced the arc in September 2024, and the anime followed suit in April this year. For the first time in anime history, One Piece has taken a seasonal schedule to maintain the quality of the animation.

Furthermore, even though a trailer hasn’t been released yet, t he God Valley film is expected to be the best film in One Piece ‘s history . Over the decades, the anime has released 15 feature-length movies and continues to carry on its legacy with more updates. This is the first time in One Piece ‘s history that the anime has ever decided to release a canon movie. So far, every film the anime has released has followed the original script from the animation studio. However, this is all the more reason why expectations for the anime movie are even higher.

The God Valley Incident is easily the best flashback in the series ever. What starts out as Harald's past, turns into an epic journey that unraveled the biggest mystery behind the incident 38 years ago. However, the fights in the manga pale in comparison to what fans usually get. This is even more disappointing considering that all the legendary figures were present on the island. Instead of focusing on the fights, the story relied more on the lore buildup. However, the movie can turn things around by highlighting the battle scenes in a much better way.

While the backstory introduced the God Valley Incident during the Wano Country Saga, the entire truth wasn’t revealed until years later in the Elbaph Arc of the manga. Not to mention that despite the fact that Kuma’s POV shed some light on the issue, the truth was far more shocking than fans ever realized. The mystery behind the historic incident was finally solved after the introduction of Rocks D. Xebec , a legendary pirate who was at the center of the chaos 38 years ago. Rocks was portrayed as an evil pirate and the instigator behind the incident, but the truth was far from it.

Not only does this flashback depict the true horrors committed by the World Government, but it also reveals how Rocks got entangled in the mess. The backstory revealed the truth behind his lineage and his son, Marshall D. Teach. Apart from the major plot twists, the backstory also includes some of the most intense fights in the series, which makes it all the more worthwhile.

What are your thoughts on the manga fights that took place during the God Valley Incident? Or you can tell us your expectations for the anime movie in the comments below.

articles.title: Classroom of the Elite Season 5 Confirms 2027 Release With First Look Trailer - Watch
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Lerche Only a few months after the fourth season's finale, the anime is all set to return next year with a new season. Classroom of the Elite Season 4 aired its final episode in June this year and reached its conclusion after setting up the major events that will take place in the future. Luckily, the anime […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Only a few months after the fourth season's finale, the anime is all set to return next year with a new season. Classroom of the Elite Season 4 aired its final episode in June this year, and while it did have a much longer extended run than previous seasons , it has come to an end with some major teases for the future. Luckily for fans, it was quickly confirmed that Classroom of the Elite Season 5 has been revealed to be in the works following its Season 4 finale. While there are few details about what to expect so far, you can check out the announcement teaser for the next season below.

2027 is going to be yet another exciting year for anime fans, maybe even better than this year. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 season , which is only a few weeks away, but a lot of the incredible series will be released throughout the year. One of Crunchyroll ‘s biggest anime franchises has confirmed the release date for its new season, and has revealed some huge plans for its premiere. Crunchyroll has a lot of franchises that anime fans will want to check out with the streaming service this year , and fans have already gotten to see a big wave as part of the Winter 2026 anime schedule. As fans gear up for the next wave of new anime coming later this Spring, one of the biggest franchises has now confirmed its release date with some big plans for its first episodes.

Classroom of the Elite  Season 5 has been announced to be in the works, but has yet to confirm a release window or date as of the time of this writing. The potential production staff or returning voice cast have yet to be revealed as of this announcement either, but getting a confirmation of a new season at all is a big show of faith for the anime moving forward. The past two seasons  have been developed and released in quick succession  compared to the years long wait between the first and second seasons.

Classroom of the Elite had been dormant for five years following the end of the first season, and returned for not only a second season, but a third and fourth as well. Now that a fifth season has been announced, it’s clear that the series is showing no signs of slowing down anytime soon for Kadokawa. That’s especially true as Ayanokoji and the others are now in the midst of their second year in school as of the end of the fourth season.

Classroom of the Elite  Season 4 ends its adaptation of the  first half of the 2nd year for Ayanokoji and the others , and with it introduced a whole new group of rivals that the class now has to deal with in order to make it to the top of the food chain. They had been successful in surviving the first year, but this is an entirely new tier of challenger that even a genius like Ayanokoji has been having to work that much harder to out think and overcome in his schemes so far.

You’re going to need to be sure to catch up with everything now streaming with Crunchyroll in the meantime. Classroom of the Elite is a lot of complicated schemes and tricks that sometimes don’t completely make sense, so you’ll need to pay close attention to the character choices and dialogue in order to keep on top of everything. It seems there might be plenty of time to do so before Season 5.

Are you caught up with all episodes of Classroom of the Elite on Crunchyroll? Head down to the comments to let us know your expectations for Season 5.

articles.summary: JAFF Market, which organizers bill as Indonesia's biggest film market, opened its third edition at the Jogja Expo Center in Yogyakarta with market director Linda Gozali urging the local industry to judge its growth on quality as well as scale. The three-day market runs alongside the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF). Gozali said the first […]
articles.content:
JAFF Market , which organizers bill as Indonesia's biggest film market, opened its third edition at the Jogja Expo Center in Yogyakarta with market director Linda Gozali urging the local industry to judge its growth on quality as well as scale.

The three-day market runs alongside the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF). Gozali said the first edition was conceived as an experiment. "It is actually a question that we threw into the Indonesian ecosystem whether or not we truly need a film market. And the response was definitely overwhelming," she said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Huw Edwards Speaks Publicly About Conviction and Downfall for First Time in Channel 4 Doc: 'I'd Lost the Plot' Princess Kate Cancer Documentary ‘Heal’ Sets BBC, NBC and International Premiere Dates

Gozali said the market's third outing called for some reflection on whether the industry can "actually endure and survive the economic upheaval, the socio-political instability, as well as whatever issues that are actually evolving in the global era."

The 2025 edition centered on local and international collaboration, she said, with the goal of turning leads into multiple deals.

"This is a transitional period, and therefore let's define what growth is," Gozali added. "We have to define growth not just in terms of the quantity, no. Because growth in quantity itself will reduce at a time where there are challenges around the environment. So we look at growth as well from the quality point of view."

The exhibition floor hosts 116 exhibitors, and the opening day was reserved as a business day for accredited badge holders. Amar Bank is powering the market for the second year running.

The JAFF Future Project selection comprises 12 projects. Indonesian titles are Dhiwangkara Seta's "Absence" (stylized "αLPα"), Timoteus Anggawan Kusno's "Orphaned Atlas" (an Indonesia-France-Netherlands co-production), "Pupus: The Orchid of Merapi," "A Quiet Sunshine," "Somewhere Between" and Sidharta Tata's "Slaughterground," along with "Gokil," presented with Jakarta Film Week. From elsewhere come Glenn Barit's "Luz and Flor" (Philippines), Rein Maychaelson's "Primal" (Indonesia, Singapore, South Korea), M. Raihan Halim's "The Smuggler" (Singapore), Boo Junfeng's multi-country co-production "Trinity" and Rosie Lourde's "Wreck and Ruin" (Australia), which arrives via a partnership with the Adelaide Film Festival and Malaysia's mylab. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The IP Connection strand, formerly known as JAFF Content Market, has opened to international properties for the first time. Of its 10 selections, four come from overseas: the comic "Disposable Dolly" (Hong Kong), the book "Cat Rental Company" (Taiwan) and two South Korean titles brought in through a partnership with Busan's Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the book "My Upstairs Neighbors" and the webtoon "Friend Request." The six Indonesian properties are animation "Komarong," board game "Mantra," comics "Blood Upon the Snow," "Lao Sam 1892" and "Yuuko's Gloomy Days," and novel "Hati-Hati Ada Dua Hati" (roughly, "Watch Out, There Are Two Hearts").

Among the new initiatives is a Producers Exchange, whose first batch numbers 14 producers: Lisa Scott and Rae Choi (Australia), who come via the Adelaide Film Festival, Jason Karman (Canada, Indonesia), Nana Riskhi and Nick Musa (Indonesia), Wong Kew Soon (Malaysia), Otgontuya Zorig (Mongolia), Danzen Santos Katanyag (Philippines), Sam Chua Weishi and Wendy Lie (Singapore), Kimbo Kim (South Korea), Shao-Yi Chen (Taiwan), Phimphloi Nan Saensuk (Thailand) and Rajib Mohajan (Bangladesh, U.S.). Chua is pulling double duty: she is also one of the producers of "Primal."

The Indonesia-France Film Lab X MTN Lab, now in its third year, is run by the French Embassy and the Institut français d'Indonésie (IFI), with Paris film school La Fémis supplying the mentors. Indonesian partners include the Ministry of Culture's Directorate of Film, Music and Arts, whose national talent management program MTN gives the lab its name, along with the Indonesia Film Agency (BPI) and the Association of Indonesian Film Producers (Aprofi). This year's six projects, all debut or sophomore features from director-producer pairings, are "A Straight Way to Love," "An Interesting Incident," "Father Figure," "My Tears, a Sea for Jakarta to Sink," "Saltstorm!" and "Super Neli."

A second new program focuses on film writing across journalism, criticism and the essay form. It has 15 young participants, among them journalists, writers, lecturers, researchers and communications professionals.

The first day's conference program includes a big-ideas session on where Indonesian cinema goes next, along with a session on how cultural phenomena can grow beyond trends and open doors to cross-border projects. The second day will turn to the question of where the country's audience actually sits, with Gozali noting that many foreign collaborators arrive drawn by the "lucrative Indonesian market." Sessions that day will also cover AI in microdramas, documentaries, budgets and what it takes for an Indonesian production house to last 30 years. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Economically speaking, we are actually in a cautious mood," Gozali said.

The final day will take in animation, box office breakouts and actors who have moved into producing, plus a talk on action and stunts from Japanese action director Tanigaki Kenji.

Ahmad Mahendra, director general of culture development, utilization and fostering at Indonesia's Ministry of Culture, delivered a brief keynote in which he said he hoped the market would keep growing and strengthening the country's film ecosystem, and that the ministry could lend its support. The market was then declared open as guests inserted memory sticks into a projector.

Joining Mahendra on stage were JAFF founder Garin Nugroho , festival director Ifa Isfansyah, JAFF Market executive director Ajish Dibyo, business director Sekarini Seruni, business strategist FX Iwan, board members Lorna Tee and Yulia Evina Bhara, and Amar Bank senior VP Josua Sloane. French ambassador to Indonesia Fabien Penone also attended, along with Cecep Rukendi, deputy for media creativity at the Ministry of Creative Economy, and Andhika Permata, head of Jakarta's Tourism and Creative Economy Agency.

"People say the third is the charm," Gozali said. "Hopefully it is, fingers crossed."

Indian auteur Anurag Kashyap ("Gangs of Wasseypur") and producer Ranjan Singh have boarded " The Melody of Destiny ," a short film rooted in the northern Indian state of Haryana, as presenters and executive producers, backing the film on the festival circuit.

The short is the first film from Chaitanya Chugh, a 24-year-old self-taught director from Pehowa, Haryana. He produced it with Diya Panjwani and Aabhar S Dev. Saurabh Bansal plays Rajesh, who lives in Delhi, far from his wife and daughter in Haryana, and sings on the city's streets in secret. He is saving for the day his daughter Priya (Miraya Sehgal), 10, gets married. She lives at home with her mother, Savitri (Nagmeet Arora). One evening, a conversation over dinner turns into a fight, and the family's strained relationships come out into the open. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Chugh shot the film guerrilla-style on Delhi's streets. The idea came from two moments in his own life after the COVID-19 lockdown. In 2021, his mother told him she had given a saree from her wedding to a street performer who was collecting money for his daughter's marriage. Months later, on the way to the mountains, Chugh saw a roadside banner offering 51 wedding items for INR 51,000 ($530), and the two memories came together.

"Initially drawn from the stark reality of the importance of marriages in India, which is maligned by the illegal practice of dowry, it grew into an exploration of gendered roles and power, and how they shape family dynamics, especially in traditional setups. By looking into a household whose relationships are governed by abuse rooted in the problems of class and patriarchy, the film tries to present a documentation of these gruesome truths," Chugh said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Most of the crew was female. The film also draws on Haryanvi folklore, which traditionally tells stories through metaphor in song.

"The film really punches you hard at one point," Kashyap said. "Chaitanya really knows the world that he has captured intimately in the film. It's powerful, it's sensitive and carries some really authentic performances. I hope the film travels far and wide."

Singh said it is rare to see a young filmmaker try to push boundaries with a first film, adding that Chugh "does that convincingly in 'The Melody of Destiny.' He definitely has a unique storytelling approach and an emotional outlook which is a must for this story. I saw the film through one of the producers Diya, and strongly felt it's a film that should be taken to the world, and thus happy to onboard the film and try and do the same."

articles.title: 5 Marvel Legacy Villains Who Became Legends in Their Own Right and One Got a Wild MCU Makeover
articles.summary: Marvel Comics has been defining what superhero stories could be for decades, leading to the massive success that was the MCU. Marvel started with the superhero in 1939, but wouldn't hit the highest heights until the '60s. While the House of Ideas did have a legacy that stretched back to the Golden Age, legacy never […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics has been defining what superhero stories could be for decades, leading to the massive success that was the MCU. Marvel started with the superhero in 1939, but wouldn't hit the highest heights until the '60s. While the House of Ideas did have a legacy that stretched back to the Golden Age, legacy never really felt important to the Marvel Universe the way it did the DC Multiverse. DC felt generational, whereas Marvel just felt like a long unfolding now. However, that doesn't mean legacy wasn't a factor; numerous legacy heroes have took the fire of the past into the present, many battling legacy villains.

Legacy villains are as important to the Marvel Universe as legacy heroes. They have linked past and present beautifully and some of them have become major villains, battling against the greatest heroes ever. These five Marvel legacy villains all became legends, some outstripping what came before, and one of them had the wildest MCU reinvention ever.

The Krakoa Era redefined the X-Men , taking them out of the mansion and putting them in their own mutant nation, bringing together heroes and villains. However, put a bunch of mutants together and someone is going to start building Sentinels, with the Orchis Initiative inheriting the various anti-mutant agencies of the world. Their first goal was to create a Nimrod unit. The first Nimrod unit came from the future, where Sentinel technology had been perfected. Nimrods were the ultimate Sentinel and it was thought to be impossible to build one in the present. Orchis was stopped by the X-Men, but eventually, they succeeded, basing his mind off the mind of the slain Orchis security chief.

This new Nimrod was an improvement in every way. He was more powerful, battling the most powerful mutants to the death, and led Orchis against Krakoa alongside Omega Sentinel and Dr. Stasis. He was everything you wanted a villain to be – powerful, scary, and cool-looking. Usually, Sentinels aren't all that interesting, but Nimrod was able to escape that fate and become one of the best legacy villains ever.

On the one hand, Carnage has always been one of those villains who seemed too simple to actually be interesting. Cletus Kasady was a serial killer who lucked out, sharing a cell with Eddie Brock. He was planning on killing his new cellie, but the Venom symbiote broke Brock out, leaving a piece of itself behind. He bonded with it and became Carnage. Since then, the symbiotic psychopath has been one of the simplest villains in the Marvel Universe – he's a powerful killer who usually is able to amass quite a body count before getting taken down. He's gotten more powerful over the years as well, even helming his own events.

Carnage is here not because he's such a great villain, but because of how popular he was. He proved that the success of Venom wasn't a fluke and that symbiotes were a viable way of creating new villains. His stories aren't usually very deep or anything and all of them are basically the same, but he's become one of the most popular Spider-Man villains of them all. His success is one reason there are so many symbiotes, showing that it was a character-type with legs.

Marvel is full of irredeemable villains and even among that number, Red Skull is something special in the worst possible way. Johann Schmidt is a Nazi, having been personally selected by Adolf Hitler to be the Reich's most dangerous soldier. He and Captain America became arch-foes over the course of the war, but only one of them walked out of it, with Red Skull in control of Hydra and the remnants of the Nazi war machine after the death of his Fuhrer. He created a Reich in the shadows, building his strength until he could attack the world again. During this period, he fathered a child, the little girl who would become Sin.

Sin was raised by Mother Night, the evil nun who taught the gospel of Red Skull, trained to be just as monstrous as her father. Once she got old enough, she joined her father's battle against Cap, working closely with Crossbones, eventually entering into a relationship with him. The two of them became the field leaders of Red Skull's army and she would even take her father's place for a time, carving the flesh off her face. Sin doesn't get a lot of attention anymore but she's one of the best of all time.

Spider-Man started his adventures as a teen, battling against the likes of Doctor Octopus and Green Goblin, then doing homework after their fights. He'd start to make more friends as he got older and eventually forged a friendship with Harry Osborn, the son of industrialist Norman Osborn. Norman had another secret as well – he was the Green Goblin. He would die in battle with the Wall-Crawler and years later, Harry would discover the truth. The Osborn madness gripped him and he became a new Green Goblin, using his father's weapons against his best friend before getting his hands on the Goblin formula.

This would lead to his death, dying in battle with Spidey because of his new superpowers. Harry as Green Goblin was honestly better than Norman. His and Peter's relationship was even closer, so watching it fall apart and Harry fall to evil was amazing. J.M. DeMatteis and Sal Buscema's Spectacular Spider-Man run is worth reading for numerous reasons but one of the best of them is easily Harry as the Goblin.

Captain America's first villains were a mixed bag , but one of the best was always Henreich Zemo. The former Nazi baron battled Cap back in World War II, responsible for the hero's hibernation and Bucky becoming the Winter Soldier, and would join Hydra in the intervening years. He also had a son Helmut and when Cap returned, Henreich went after him again, battling him and the Avengers, forming the Masters of Evil before dying. Helmut would follow in his father's footsteps and became the new Baron Zemo, quickly becoming one of the most dangerous villains in the Marvel Universe.

Zemo was known for his master planning and leadership skills, but he was no slouch in combat either, battling numerous superpowered foes to a standstill. He was brought into the MCU and completely changed; he was established as a special forces soldier and then was made into something of a goof, which is a time-honored MCU tradition – stay there long enough and you'll become a clown as well. However, the real Zemo is a menace, challenging the greatest heroes in the Marvel Universe in a way his father could have only dreamed of.

articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Ufotable Rengoku's voice actor shares his thoughts on the most iconic anime moment ever. The Demon Slayer: Mugen Train film hit the Japanese theaters on October 16th, 2020, and it made history with its astounding success. Before the anime adaptation was premiered in 2019, the manga had over 3.5 million copies in circulation, which increased to 10 million […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Rengoku's voice actor shares his thoughts on the most iconic anime moment ever. The Demon Slayer : Mugen Train film was released in Japanese theaters on October 16th, 2025, and it made history with its astounding success. Before the anime adaptation was released in 2019, the manga had over 3.5 million copies in circulation, which increased to 10 million in September, around the time of the first season’s finale. The manga continued to rise through the charts, eventually hitting the 100 million milestone about two weeks before Mugen Train ‘s premiere. The series could already be considered at the peak of its popularity, but Mugen Train ‘s groundbreaking success etched its name into anime history. The film surpassed the long-standing box office records of classics such as Makoto Shinkai’s Your Name and Studio Ghibli’s Spirited Away .

After the release of the Infinity Castle film this year , both Demon Slayer films now rank as the top two among the highest-grossing Japanese films of all time. The film’s success also somewhat influenced Ufotable’s decision to make a trilogy for the Infinity Castle Arc , which turned out for the best. However, Mugen Train ‘s success isn’t only thanks to the flashy animation but also the thrilling fight scenes and emotional weight. The arc was only 13 chapters long in the manga, and yet it completely changed the course of the story.

As per Oricon, he shares, “It was a night of fierce battles between Tanjiro and his friends against Enmu, and between Rengoku Kyojuro and Akaza, which was short in time but felt incredibly long. I remember feeling a great sense of responsibility as I recorded, knowing that this one night's battle would have great significance for Tanjiro and his friends going forward.”

He added, “I'm sure many people, like Tanjiro, were encouraged by the words 'Burn Your Heart,' which are also in the title of episode seven. I myself am one of them. I was happy to be able to look back on the time of the Mugen Train with everyone again through the rebroadcast!”

The fight between Rengoku and Akaza isn’t the best because of the thrilling action or the fight choreography, but because of the impact it had on the overall story . His final words, “Set your heart ablaze,” simply mean having a strong desire to work towards one’s goal even in the face of adversity. His death was a reminder to Tanjiro and the others that they were truly too weak to protect everyone. This is all the more reason why Rengoku’s death sparked a new flame in the three rookie Demon Slayers , who swore to continue moving forward, even if they were sad or filled with regret.

They dedicated themselves to training and strived to become stronger, especially Tanjiro, who didn’t want to let anyone down as he did with Rengoku. Tanjiro carried the guard of Kyojuro’s sword with him as a reminder of his determination and his desire to be like the Flame Hashira. The determination that he gained thanks to Rengoku’s sacrifice stayed with him until the end of the story, shaping his journey going forward.

Do you think Demon Slayer has another fight that has a similar level of emotional impact? Or you can head down to the comments to share your favorite fight in the series.

articles.title: 3 More New Anime to Watch If You Miss 1990s Anime
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Arvo Animation The 1990s were a revolutionary decade for the anime industry, and it's even more impossible to recreate the aesthetic visuals and storytelling now. The decade introduced several iconic movies and series that are appreciated to this day. The 1990s not only had a distinctive style with grainy visuals, but the unforgettable music made every watch […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There’s no denying that the 1990s was a revolutionary decade for the anime industry, as it introduced several iconic films and series that are still loved even now. The animation styles were distinctive, with grainy visuals that can’t be replicated today. The music was unforgettable, and each story had a unique plot to offer, which made these shows and movies even more unforgettable. However, it’s not just the plot or visuals that make these series special, as fans often have an emotional attachment to some of their childhood favorites . It was an era before streaming platforms became popular, but several Japanese anime series were made accessible worldwide thanks to TV channels in English-dubbed formats.

Anime is now a mainstream form of media, pulling in more viewers over the years. Since it’s often overwhelming to find the right anime to start with, many beginners would turn to a series that recently went popular. Unfortunately, a majority of these newer series have a completely different vibe than the 1990s. While the stunning beauty of the 1990s can’t be recreated today , there are plenty of newer series that will remind you of that era. Keep in mind this list doesn’t include reboots of older classics with the same plot but with modern animation.

The best spooky anime Netflix has to offer is none other than its exclusive  Cyberpunk: Edgerunners,  based on the popular video game franchise  Cyberpunk  2077. The anime captures the perfect sci-fi and spooky vibe of Night City from the game, presenting characters immersed in its most compelling elements. As an original anime, it is exceptionally well-written, with characters’ actions impacting others in ways that are bound to make fans cry as they watch the narrative unfold.

Across just 10 episodes, this anime is scary, dark, emotional, and occasionally funny, making it perfect not just for its spooky elements but also for its overall vibe. However, the biggest reason fans should watch it is that the anime’s second season is arriving on October 20 . While the two seasons aren’t directly connected, as the second will feature its own narrative, watching the first season will reveal what makes this anime so amazing and why it won the Anime of the Year award. With the Netflix exclusive Cyberpunk: Edgerunners returning with a new season this October, there honestly can’t be a better anime to watch on the streaming platform.

Set in early 1990s London, the story follows Lili Ichijouin, who traveled all the way from Japan to enroll in the prestigious Saint Thomas Art Academy. However, her parents wouldn’t let her continue her studies if she didn’t rank at the top of her class. Despite the pressure, she tries her best to make her dream of becoming a painter a reality. As she’s driven by her desperation and passion, she meets Kit Church, a gifted student known not only for his talent but also for his detachment from others.

Watching Kit being completely devoted to painting sparks sincerity and resilience in Lili as well, as she tries to perform better. As the two continue to get to know more about each other, they share more than just their love for art. This romantic story puts them through the challenge of breaking free from societal norms and embracing their true selves despite the opposition from everyone around them.

Kowloon Generic Romance  is the exact opposite of what its title might suggest, combining a romance story with sci-fi mystery elements. The anime was released in 2025 and already had a live-action adaptation debut this year as well.  Kowloon Generic Romance  boasts a gorgeous, detailed art style that encapsulates the nostalgia of early 2000s romance series, while adding a touch of modernity through the application of subverting tropes at every turn. If you’re into unsettling, mysterious atmospheres combined with relatable characters falling in love, this show is absolutely for you.

The story of Kowloon Generic Romance is set in the high-tech, futuristic Kowloon Walled City. Real estate agents Reiko and Hajime work within the city bounds together and are engaging in the beginnings of an office romance. In the background of this seemingly innocent dynamic, Reiko begins to notice strange peculiarities surrounding her relationship with Hajime that result in her poking around about her past. When Reiko’s reality begins to seem less and less real, she discovers a haunting secret about a past version of herself that seems to have existed before she can remember.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime in mind that you want to add here? Share your recommendations in the comments below.

articles.title: Netflix's 'Secrets' Takes Indonesian Auteur Ravi Bharwani Into Thriller Territory After Eight-Year Gap
articles.summary: Indonesian filmmaker Ravi Bharwani's Netflix thriller "Secrets," his first feature in eight years, will world premiere at the 21st Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival on Nov. 29, four days before it begins streaming on the platform on Dec. 3. Sha Ine Febriyanti ("This Earth of Mankind") plays Parni, a former sex worker who now runs a […]
articles.content:
Indonesian filmmaker Ravi Bharwani 's Netflix thriller " Secrets ," his first feature in eight years, will world premiere at the 21st Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival on Nov. 29, four days before it begins streaming on the platform on Dec. 3.

Sha Ine Febriyanti ("This Earth of Mankind") plays Parni, a former sex worker who now runs a beauty salon while raising her daughter on her own. Her hard-won stability is upended when Jamal (Abimana Aryasatya, "Gundala"), the violent man she once escaped, gets out of prison and comes back determined to reclaim her. Shenina Cinnamon plays Parni's daughter Riska, and Ruth Marini plays Darsi. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories The Killers Guitarist Dave Keuning Survived 'Major Stroke' With '40% Chance of Survival': 'I Can Play Guitar Just as Good as Before'

The film is adapted from Dewi Kharisma Michellia's short story "Rahasia dari Kramat Tunggak" ("Secrets from Kramat Tunggak"). Its early section unfolds in 1980s Jakarta, in a milieu drawn from the Kramat Tunggak district, before the story leaps ahead to the 2000s and Jamal's return. Bharwani co-wrote the screenplay with Rayya Makarim, who has worked with him for over a quarter century, and Wilza Lubis produced through Buddy Buddy Pictures. Both were also on board for his previous feature, 2018's "27 Steps of May."

Bharwani, whose earlier features are "Impian Kemarau" (2004) and "Fishing Platform" (2008), tells Variety he spent the intervening years writing scripts and synopses, completing a couple of screenplays along the way. "But then my biggest problem is still funding, distribution, so that's my biggest challenge," he says. "And simply, this is the one that got financed, so I jumped in without having to wait for another few years anymore." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

He was first drawn to the short story by a scene in which a woman is won in a game of chess. "I can feel the mood of the scene, the setting, the color, and the stickiness, the humidity of that scene," Bharwani says.

"Secrets" is his first thriller, and with it come erotic scenes, violence and action, none of which he had filmed before. He says exploring the darker side of human psychology, tackling domestic violence and working at the scale of a Netflix production made the shift difficult. That difficulty was also what drew him in.

"For me, it's not just about the bombastic scenes or the sensationalism," he says. "For me, it's how to make the audience invest in the fear, in the anger, in the hate, in being a victim, being in power of this character."

Bharwani set the opening in the 1980s because brothels in Kramat Tunggak operated legally then. The district was later shut down, though he notes the trade simply moved underground, and the area no longer exists. His research drew on a book about Kramat Tunggak and on Michael Glawogger's 2011 documentary "Whores' Glory," which follows sex workers in several countries.

"And then I do not try to be consistent, to be true to the setting of the 1980s, but what is important for the film, and that's the one that I go along with," Bharwani says. He worked closely with cinematographer Arief Retno Pribadi on color, costume and lighting so that each scene's look matched its emotional register.

Shaping Jamal meant ongoing conversations with Aryasatya through prep, the shoot and post-production. Bharwani says the actor has an uncle he recognized as a near-exact match for the character and grew up in a tough environment steeped in machismo, yet brings a real sensitivity to emotion and to women.

"There are moments that we see this is too human that we see, 'Okay, the audience will get into giving more sympathy for Jamal,'" Bharwani says. "So we need to edit it out, but at the same time not wanting to make him a one-dimensional character."

Indonesia is one of Asia's largest and fastest-growing theatrical markets, but much of that growth has come from horror and other genre fare. Bharwani says his previous work relied on international festival funding that took years to secure, and the films sometimes ended up playing only at festivals. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"So hopefully with Netflix over here, they spearhead the whole industry, change the whole industry setting of not just going to safe areas, going to horror, going to drama, or going to easier comedy films," he says.

At JAFF, "Secrets" plays in the Indonesian Screen Awards section. Editor Harin Paesongthai, production designer Menfo Tantono and composers Aghi Narottama and Tony Merle round out the key crew. Beyond promoting the film, Bharwani plans to work through the festival lineup and meet other filmmakers.

He already has projects in the writing stage. "Making a film for me is a great chance to be able to express what I feel about humans, about environment, about stuff that I experience myself," he says.

By his count, he has enough material ready for two or three more films – if someone is willing to make them.

articles.title: Jason Iskandar's 'First Breath After Coma' Revisits Lunar New Year's Public Return to Indonesia After a Three-Decade Ban, First Looks Unveiled (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Indonesian filmmaker Jason Iskandar's "First Breath After Coma," a drama set as the country's Chinese community prepared to celebrate the Lunar New Year openly for the first time in more than 30 years, has revealed first-look images of its three leads. The stills were unveiled at Indonesia's JAFF Market, which takes place alongside the 21st […]
articles.content:
Indonesian filmmaker Jason Iskandar 's " First Breath After Coma ," a drama set as the country's Chinese community prepared to celebrate the Lunar New Year openly for the first time in more than 30 years, has revealed first-look images of its three leads.

The stills were unveiled at Indonesia's JAFF Market , which takes place alongside the 21st Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF) in Yogyakarta. They show Ladya Cheryl, Morgan Oey and Abby Latip as three siblings who find their way back to one another in Jakarta at the turn of the millennium. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories The Killers Guitarist Dave Keuning Survived 'Major Stroke' With '40% Chance of Survival': 'I Can Play Guitar Just as Good as Before'

Written and directed by Iskandar and produced by Florence Giovani for Jakarta outfit Studio Antelope, the film follows a Chinese-Indonesian family during a period of national transition, in the days before Chinese New Year in 2000. That holiday was the first to be marked after the government formally dropped the curbs on public displays of Chinese culture.

From 1967 to 1998, Indonesia tightly limited how Chinese culture could be expressed in public. The New Year festivities, the Chinese language and other customs survived largely behind closed doors, kept alive within families. By 2000, those traditions were starting to resurface.

"When the restrictions were lifted, their effects did not simply disappear. They remained in everyday life, in ways that I feel are often overlooked. That is why I wanted to approach this history through a family. Through the relationships between these three siblings, we can see how our personal lives are intertwined with a much larger history. As a Chinese Indonesian, I feel that even the most personal things are already political," said Iskandar. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In one image, Cheryl grips a microphone at home, apparently in the middle of a karaoke session, a favorite pastime among Chinese Indonesians.

Oey sports period glasses and hair, with a car of the era visible behind him.

Latip wears a red cheongsam and stands among New Year lanterns, though her face suggests unease.

Cheryl won the best actress Citra Award at the 2022 Indonesian Film Festival (FFI) for "Vengeance Is Mine, All Others Pay Cash," which also won the Golden Leopard at Locarno. Oey starred in "Ghost in the Cell," which world premiered in the Berlinale's Forum strand this year. The film marks the feature debut of Latip, who appeared in the short "The Rootless Bloom," a competition title at the 28th Busan International Film Festival in 2023.

The project has been a long time coming. It began at the SGIFF Southeast Asian Film Lab in Singapore in 2015 and later went through EAVE Ties That Bind (2023/2024) in Taiwan and Italy. It was pitched at the Golden Horse Film Project Promotion (FPP) in 2024 and at the Hong Kong-Asia Film Financing Forum (HAF) in 2025.

Giovani, Iskandar's filmmaking partner since their early shorts, said the pair spent more than a decade developing the film. "As a Chinese Indonesian, I saw parts of my own life in this family's story, and that personal connection is a big part of why I wanted to help Jason bring his vision to the screen. The bond between the siblings and the pull of home are things I think audiences will recognize wherever they're from. Over the years, we found collaborators in Indonesia and across the region who connected with the story in their own ways and helped us make the film," she said.

Those collaborators include Singaporean cinematographer Teck Siang Lim ("Ah Girl," "Crocodile Tears," "Whether the Weather Is Fine") and production designer Dita Gambiro ("Four Seasons in Java," "Sore: A Wife From the Future," "Cigarette Girl"). To recreate the period, the team hunted for Jakarta locations that still look much as they did in the late 1990s, and found that some corners of the city have barely changed.

Co-producers are Yulia Evina Bhara of KawanKawan Media, Wanyi Pratiknyo and Hannan Cinthya of Arungi Films. Bhara's "Autobiography" debuted in Venice's Horizons section in 2022, and she co-produced "Tiger Stripes," winner of the Cannes Critics' Week Grand Prize in 2023. Pratiknyo co-produced "Levitating," which played in Sundance's World Cinema Dramatic Competition this year, while Cinthya was a co-producer on Next Step Studio Indonesia, a four-short program that screened at Cannes Critics' Week this year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The film is in post-production and aiming for a festival premiere in 2027, to be followed by theatrical releases in Indonesia and select international territories. The film's local title is "Perayaan Pertama."

"First Breath After Coma" follows Iskandar's 2021 debut feature "Akhirat: A Love Story," a romantic fantasy made by Studio Antelope with Base Entertainment and Ivanhoe Pictures. It opened in Indonesian theaters that December. Iskandar and Giovani founded Studio Antelope in 2011. The company has since moved into series, including "CinLock: Love, Camera, Action" for Vision+ and Netflix, and in October released Fajar Nugros' "Bapak Paling Jujur" in local cinemas.

Yogyakarta is familiar ground for the director. His short "Territorial Pissings" was named best short film at JAFF in 2010.

articles.title: Thunderbolts* Star Reveals New Avengers' Place in Doomsday, And It's Perfect After That Ending
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Avengers: Doomsday actor David Harbour explained that the New Avengers bring something very different and dysfunctional to the new movie. The new movie will feature two Avengers teams battling over who deserves to be considered the Avengers, with Sam Wilson's government-backed team fighting to hold the name while the former Thunderbolts are using the name […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday actor David Harbour explained that the New Avengers bring something very different and dysfunctional to the new movie. The new movie will feature two Avengers teams battling over who deserves to be considered the Avengers, with Sam Wilson's government-backed team fighting to hold the name while the former Thunderbolts are using the name with a "Z" after Valentina Allegra de Fontaine introduced them as the New Avengers at the end of the Thunderbolts* movie . Harbour's comments are perfect considering what happened in Thunderbolts*.

Harbour was speaking in an Entertainment Weekly interview with the entire cast of Avengers: Doomsday, and he said, "We’re there to bring our neuroses and our problems and our depression right to Captain America or Ant-Man."

While it wasn't a huge box-office success compared to other MCU movies, Thunderbolts* remains one of the best movies Marvel released after Avengers: Endgame . Directed by Jake Schreier, who has also signed on to direct the upcoming X-Men movie for the MCU, Thunderbolts* took some of the most broken and emotionally devastated heroes in Marvel, and it ended up as the formation of a found family. This was all highlighted by Florence Pugh, who plays Yelena Belova, the character who Kevin Feige has said is the character anchoring Avengers: Doomsday .

Looking at Sam Wilson's team, that Avengers lineup looks like a well-oiled team, even though we have never seen them working together before. Shang-Chi hasn't been seen since his solo movie, although there was a mid-credits scene where he was speaking with Wong, Carol Danvers, and Bruce Banner, showing that he has experience with some MCU heavyweights. The other members are Joaquin Torres' Falcon, who worked with Sam and Bucky in The Falcon and the Winter Soldier , and Ant-Man, who was there to fight with the Avengers in Avengers: Endgame . While we haven't seen them fighting together, they are all proven heroes.

However, the New Avengers are the most dysfunctional team in the MCU, and that is what makes them even more entertaining. Honestly, Sam's team is boring, even with Ant-Man's comedy, while the former Thunderbolts are so quirky that they should steal every scene they are in. Yelena Belova is someone who can connect the New Avengers to the rest of the MCU thanks to her relationship with Natasha Romanoff, and Bucky is as close to Sam as he is to anyone in the world other than Steve Rogers. Add in Ghost, Red Guardian, U.S. Agent, and Sentry, and there is a lot about this team that should play into the new movie.

While Yelena Belova might be the anchor and Bucky is the team veteran, the New Avengers member to watch out for here is Sentry. Right now, Bob only wants to be a background character because he is scared he might lose control as the Void again. That is likely what will happen. In the comics, Doctor Doom used the Molecule Man to help him create Battleworld, and it could be interesting to see what happens if Doom convinces Sentry to switch sides for the greater good.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A 13-year-old game from the late PS3 and Xbox 360 era is finally coming to a Nintendo platform with a new release on the Nintendo Switch this Sunday, November 29. For those who do not know, a Sunday release is peculiar and extraordinarily rare, making the release even more noteworthy. There's no Nintendo Switch 2 version releasing alongside this Switch version, so those on the newer Nintendo console will have to settle for accessing the game through backward compatibility. That said, anyone who wants to play the game on Switch on November 29 will need to fork over $24.99.

In addition to a new free game , this weekend Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 users will be able to check out The Wolf Among Us Remastered . The Wolf Among Us debuted all the way back in 2013. At the time, the Wii U was the primary Nintendo console. Many games skipped the Wii U, and this was no exception. Back on October 29, a remaster of the game was released on all modern platforms, minus Nintendo platforms again. Now, this is being remedied.

The original game was notably developed and published by Telltale Games. It's an episodic adventure game, so each episode has its own Metacritic score, but generally the game earned 80s. It's not among 2013's best games, but it was a bit of a sleeper hit with a cult following. After more than a decade, it's getting a sequel from the new Telltale Games, which is not the original Telltale Games. The original shut down. This is a different company, but it's the same name and owns much of Telltale's IP. This sequel is no doubt why the original game got remastered. And for those looking forward to the series' contnuation, the reception of the remaster is a positive sign. To this end, it has an 82 on Metacritic and notably very high user review scores .

One of 2013's Best Narrative Games The game, for those just learning about it, is an adventure game where the dialogue and action decisions you make over the course of the game influence the story and eventually lead to different endings. As for the game itself, it is based on Bill Willingham's Fables comic series, and stars Bigby Wolf, aka the Big Bad Wold. In Fabletown, where justice isn't clean, Bigby is an investigator who must get to the bottom of a string of brutal murders, which means investigating crime scenes, interrogating suspects, and eventually uncovering a dark conspiracy in a place where myths and legends live secretly among us.

As for the remaster, it mostly just enhances the visuals of the game, which is about all it needed in the first place. Gameplay is minimal. It's a narrative-driven game, and the narrative is as good in 2026 as it was in 2013.

articles.title: Christian Bale's Batman Had the Coolest Batmobile Alternative and Now It Is Being Auctioned for a Criminally High Price

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When thinking of Batman vehicles it is hard to get past the Batmobile as the most iconic of the Dark Knight's rides. That doesn't mean that the character doesn't have other ways of getting around Gotham City that are just as awesome. In 1989's Tim Burton movie, the Batwing created one of the franchise's unforgettable images when Michael Keaton's Batman flies it in front of a full moon, creating a version of the Bat Signal in the sky. Keaton also got to use the Batskiboat in Batman Returns while the Batboat was piloted by Robin in Batman Forever . Yet it was Christian Bale who had the coolest Batmobile alternative with the Batpod, a two-wheeled motorcycle that is slim and sleek and creates quite an impression blasting around the narrow alleys of the city. Fans of the Christopher Nolan-directed Batman trilogy now have the option of getting their hands on the actual vehicle used in The Dark Knight , but you may not be able to afford it on an honest wage.

Used in The Dark Knight and The Dark Knight Rises , the Batpod is used by Bale's Batman in several key scenes across the Nolan's sequels. In The Dark Knight , the Batpod is used after the Tumbler vehicles is wrecked with Batman almost driving it into Heath Ledger's Joker but diverting around him at the last moment. It is also seen in the failed attempt to rescue Maggie Gyllenhaal's Rachel and in the search for Aaron Eckhart's Harvey Dent. The vehicle was then used again in The Dark Knight Rises when Batman confronts Bane and the League of Shadows. Thanks to several distinct scratches and other markings, the Batpod has been matched to the Joker scene in The Dark Knight , which is one reason this is already bidding at $450,000 with an eye on pushing towards $1 million.

In Nolan's Dark Knight trilogy, the trusty long and iconic Batmobile is replaced with the Tumbler, an armored stocky vehicle that can blast around Gotham and withstand most attacks from the city's criminals. Designed by Nolan and production designer Nathan Crowley, the Batpod was conceived as a smaller alternate vehicle for Bale's crimefighter to use when the moment requires something slim and powerful. As well as appearing in the movie, the Batpod was also used in many promotional events for both movies, making this a very special piece of Batman history for anyone looking for their new ultimate collectible. Although it may not be the same as owning the Batmobile - the 1992 Batman Returns movie version recently sold for almost $5 million in a separate auction - owning any of the Dark Knights array of vehicles will see this one attracting a lot more bids before the hammer falls.

The custom-made Batpod is built around a Honda CRF450X engine, with 31″ Hoosier racing tyres, fibreglass body panels, plastic, resin and fibreglass twin cannon barrels at the front of the bike, a light-up laser targeting unit and a breaking system operated by the user from the handlebar controls. However, don't expect to go rocketing around the streets on this bad boy as the vehicle comes in "rolling only" condition, with the battery, fuel tank and throttle controls all having been removed. There are certainly some collectibles that would make you the envy of your friends, and this must be one of the biggest. Even without the ability to actually drive it, this is still a very rare opportunity to own one of the coolest Batman vehicles, and just being able to sit on the same seat as Christian Bale across two movies should be enough for any serious collector to reach for their wallet.

What is your favorite Batman vehicle? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Forgotten Spider-Man Villains Who Deserve a Second Chance
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Spider-Man has one of the strongest rogues galleries in comics, only rivaled by other genre-defining classics like Batman and Daredevil. Green Goblin, Venom, Doctor Octopus, and so many more have become staples who have stood at the center of some of the greatest stories Marvel has ever put to page, but they're far from the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Spider-Man has one of the strongest rogues galleries in comics , only rivaled by other genre-defining classics like Batman and Daredevil. Green Goblin, Venom, Doctor Octopus, and so many more have become staples who have stood at the center of some of the greatest stories Marvel has ever put to page, but they're far from the only foes this Wall-Crawler deals with on a bi-weekly basis. He has dozens of villains who could have just as much potential to make a big splash, but they've been relegated to a scant few appearances, if they show up at all outside of their debuts. Today, we're giving those Spider-Man villains their due and digging into what makes them so interesting. Without further ado, let's swing into Spider-Man's supervillain situation.

Vermin's life has always been on a downward spiral. First, his father abused him terribly as a child, and even after getting away from that house, he wound up being captured by Baron Zemo and experimented on, turning him into a human-rat hybrid. All of this left the man with a serious case of self-worth issues, which means that he's always manipulated or used by other supervillains in their schemes. He's a tragic villain in a way that not many of Spider-Man's most popular villains are, which could be a great platform to explore the humanity and understanding that makes Spider-Man such a great hero.

From a powers standpoint, Vermin is also one of the few who can match Spidey in terms of pure agility. He might not be as strong as Pete, but he makes up for it with ferocity and rat-like senses, which even let him command other small animals, like rats and stray dogs, to attack like a small army. Speaking of armies, Vermin also has the ability to create duplicates of himself, though when he last used this, it cost him his intellect. Overall, Vermin has perfect rat theming , which contrasts Spider-Man's spider theme in a fantastic and very entertaining way.

Digger is only one name of this undead creature, who is otherwise known as the Vegas Thirteen. He's called that because he's actually a composite being made up of different body parts from thirteen of the deadliest, evilest crime bosses and their lieutenants, stitched together and resurrected by gamma radiation. Digger is a fascinating character because he captures that classic man-out-of-time energy that makes Captain America work so well, while combining it with classic gangster style and theatrics. There's so much more potential for a concept like this than his scant few appearances, none of which dug into this as much as it deserves.

Of course, Digger also offers a unique challenge for Spider-Man, given that he's really, really strong. While not quite on the Hulk's level, Digger is on a completely different level than most of Spider-Man's other foes, to the point where Peter couldn't hurt him if he tried. This forces Spider-Man to get creative in his approach, which is always when he's at his best. The greatest Spider-Man fights involve Peter coming up with an outside-the-box solution like only he can, and this is one problem that he absolutely cannot brute force his way through.

Shathra is the Totem-eating Wasp-Goddess that hails from the same realm as Morlun, although instead of being a vampire, she's much more willing to directly consume her prey. Her ultimate goal is to destroy the Web of Life and Destiny and replace it with one of her own design, often bringing her into conflict with the various defenders of the Spider-Verse. Unlike Morlun, however, she's much more insidious in her hunts and enjoys playing with her food. The first time she battled Spider-Man, she transformed into a human woman and attempted to ruin his reputation before finally destroying him, which just goes to show that she revels in both the hunt and the cruelty she inflicts.

Much like how Spider-Man can do everything a spider can do, Shathra can do everything a moth can. She's also shown to be physically outclass Spider-Man in just about everything, possess shapeshifting powers, and is even able to infect others to join her villainous army of wasps. Shathra is a different kind of Spider-Verse monster, mixing the predatory fear that Morlun generates with the cruel, calculating cunning more akin to someone like Norman Osborn, and those two coming together, along with the great imagery of a wasp and spider fight, make her a fantastic candidate for future adventures.

Tendril started out as a man down on his luck. After a lifetime of tragedy, between his mother killing herself, his dad losing himself to mental disorders, and bouncing around foster homes, he thought he would meet his end at the hands of flesh-eating bacteria. He volunteered for experimental testing of a cure, only for Peter's own lab work to get accidentally used on him, transforming him into a monstrous form where his entire body was made of super-strong webbing. He became a spider-life figure who was practically immune to any and all physical harm, possessing all of the strengths and adaptability of Spider-Man's greatest creation amplified tenfold.

Spider-Man fighting a villain literally made of his webbing is the type of idea that's either the dumbest thing of all time or the most interesting, and either way, it definitely deserves to get explored a bit more in the future. However, as entertaining as Tendril's powers are, his real contribution to the Spider-mythos is definitely his connection to Peter. The Wall-Crawler would definitely blame himself for everything that happened, and Peter is always at his most interesting when he's grappling with his conscience on some level . This could force Peter to confront some aspects of himself that he definitely does not like, and it could be really awesome to see.

Molten Man is one of the all-time classic Spider-Man villains, debuting all the way back in The Amazing Spider-Man (1963) #28. A failed robbery ended up with Mark Raxton being coated in an experimental liquid alloy that turned his skin to gold and superheated him to the point that everything he touched burst into flames. He learned that he could control this fire, too, by shooting off massive blasts and fireballs practically whenever he wanted. He's a walking threat, given that just being near him is enough to blister your skin, and his actual touch could melt a person in seconds. Currently, he's retired, as he's been cured of his condition, but he definitely doesn't deserve to be forgotten.

See, the most interesting part about Molten Man is that he's the step-brother of longtime Spidey character Liz Allen, which opens the doors for all kinds of familial drama that I'm surprised we haven't seen yet. For example, despite Liz literally being married to Harry, we've never had a Green Goblin and Molten Man team up. There's an untapped well of potential stories here, especially considering the only things in the world that Mark cares about are his sister and finding a cure. This could easily be pushed to any number of logical extremes that would be sure to give us some wonderfully resonant stories.

Which forgotten Spider-Man villain do you think deserves more recognition? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Nick Frost plays Hagrid in the upcoming Harry Potter HBO series, and he has named two of his main inspirations for how he played the character. Neither of them is the original Hagrid actor, Robbie Coltrane. Frost is best known to fans as the actor who starred in Edgar Wright's Three Flavours Cornetto Trilogy with Simon Pegg. These movies, Shaun of the Dead , Hot Fuzz , and The World's End , made him a cult favorite, and this makes his move to the Harry Potter world such a huge step up for the actor. He is also trying to make the role his own.

In a special Q&A from the official Harry Potter website, Frost explained that there were two figures who inspired his portrayal of Hagrid in the Harry Potter HBO series. He said the two inspirations were John Coffey, the character that Michael Clarke Duncan played in the movie The Green Mile , and Frost's own Uncle Emy.

According to Frost, the first inspiration for his portrayal of Hagrid in the HBO Harry Potter series was the character John Coffey from The Green Mile . This was a movie based on a Stephen King novel about a man wrongly found guilty of murder and sentenced to die on death row. That man was John Coffey, and he was a gentle giant who had magical powers to heal others but who was willing to accept his fate despite his innocence. According to Frost, Coffey was "a very, very dangerous man, but he's essentially a big child who can be hurt."

The second inspiration is one that only Frost and his family knew about. It was his uncle, Emy. He said that Emy was a youngster in the 1950s who contracted an obscure strain of scarlet fever, and he never mentally or physically progressed past the age of 11. Frost continued by saying, "When me and my cousins spent every holiday down in Wales with him (my gran lived in this huge forest), he was like the Pied Piper. We’d just follow him around. He’d tell us stories he’d made up or take us to a den that he’d built or a little bit of river where he had dammed. Sometimes he’d have a chick in his pocket, keeping it warm. That was magic to me. I wanted Hagrid to be that."

In the Harry Potter novels, Hagrid was an innocent giant when he attended Hogwarts, and that allowed Tom Riddle (the future Voldemort) to frame him for opening the Chamber of Secrets and causing the death of a Muggle-born student, Moaning Myrtle. Hagrid's innocence and lack of intelligence didn't allow him to understand how to defend himself, and he was expelled. Luckily, Dumbledore believed in his innocence, and he convinced then-Headmaster Armando Dippet to let Hagrid remain at Hogwarts as a gamekeeper, although he was no longer allowed to legally practice magic.

Frost explained that he wanted his version of Hagrid to have the innocence that people like his Uncle Emy and John Coffey from The Green Mile exhibited. He added that Hagrid was big and strong enough to hurt someone, and he had an edge of danger to him, but he would only hurt someone if they tried to hurt anyone he cared about, like young Harry Potter.

NBC has pulled from its air a controversial ad that is critical of the United States' policy of sending financial aid to Israel . The ad ran Wednesday night during the network's Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special.

Titled "Every Three Seconds," the half-minute spot shows a young girl working to save $400 to buy a coveted bicycle. It follows her as she does such chores as moving lawns and shoveling snow until the girl proudly takes a jar filled with coins and small bills to the store. The narrator then says: "Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to do this."

A person familiar with the matter told Deadline that NBC won't re-air the ad, which comes from The IMEU Policy Project aka the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project.

articles.title: One Thing About Prime Video’s Clashing Through The Snow Really Upset Fans (Myself Included)
articles.summary: It was a near-perfect movie!
articles.content:
The holiday movies have officially taken over the 2026 TV schedule , and I could not be happier. Between Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas lineup , Netflix’s releases, and even Hulu’s 12 Dates of Christmas , the options have been endless. Now, Prime Video is getting in on the fun with the release of Clashing Through the Snow. As of writing this, the festive flick is sitting in the number three spot on the streamer’s trending charts, but don’t let the popularity fool you. Some fans are really upset that the film featured a character asking ChatGPT for relationship advice, and I agree with their outrage.

Clashing Through the Snow is overflowing with witty banter, memorable scenes, and hilarious and endearing side characters, which is why it was so upsetting when Ryan opted to ask ChatGPT for relationship advice instead of calling his friend Walter (Andrew Schulz), who had already given him advice earlier in the film.

Things weren’t much better over on Threads, where fans also made their distaste for the inclusion abundantly clear:

I don’t know what’s more upsetting: the fact that the film had a Ryan ask ChatGPT for advice or the fact that he was a senior book editor with human friends he could have turned to.

What might be the most infuriating thing is that apparently there was a version of Clashing through the Snow where Ryan did turn to a human instead of ChatGPT. At least that’s what Carlson Young, the film’s director, told Deadline before defending her decision to go with the scene in the film, saying:

Maybe I missed something, but I can’t wrap my head around hopeless romantic, pragmatic Ryan being the character who would turn to ChatGPT to ask for serious relationship help. That seems like a job he would have wanted a human who can experience actual love to help with, like Walter or even some random stranger he could have stumbled upon.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the most anticipated anime of 2027 confirmed its release date in a brand new trailer. Since fans of Vinland Saga fans still have no idea when to expect the anime's third season, this upcoming historical anime will be perfect for fans to watch in the meantime. Although it's been almost four years since the second season premiered, the creator confirmed in October that the third season still isn't under production. Lucky for fans, among the several incredible anime coming next year, Hitoshi Iwaaki’s award-winning manga,  Historie , will premiere during the Winter anime lineup of 2027.

2026 is nearing its end, which means that the upcoming series for next year are sharing new information before the year wraps up. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 lineup, as it includes highly anticipated sequels and debuts. Historie is one of the Winter 2027 anime series that you need to watch, especially if you're a fan of historical Seinen like Vinland Saga. While most international fans are most familiar with the creator because of  Parasyte ,  not many know about his underrated historical manga,  Historie . The anime released its key visual and second promotional trailer earlier this week to confirm its release date.

The latest update reveals Historie will premiere on January 8th, 2027. A key visual was also shared by the official anime website , where you can catch up with all the updates related to the series. The caption of the second promotional video also reveals the broadcast information, including the schedule for each TV network where the anime will be aired. The anime also reveals that it will be streaming on Amazon Prime Video for Japanese fans starting January 13th, after a few days of delay.

Viewers will require a membership to stream the show online every Wednesday. However, the streaming information is only for Japanese fans, as there has been no mention of global availability. The anime will likely share the streaming details for outside of Japan at least a few weeks before the premiere. Considering the hype and scale of the project, it's almost a given that the anime will definitely make its debut on international platforms.

While both stories have different narrative structures , they focus on the survival and epic journey of the protagonists. Not only that, but the themes of resilience and the coming-of-age story in Historie are something that Vinland Saga fans are sure to love. While Thorfinn’s gruesome journey centers around grief, regret, and redemption, Eumenes’s story follows his exceptional story as a brilliant strategist. Written by a legendary creator, Historie is already causing quite a lot of buzz, especially since it has a unique premise.

The manga has been serializing since 2003, and it's finally getting the attention it deserves. Set in the mid-14th century BC Greece, the story follows  a fictionalized account of Eumenes , who later became known throughout the world as the secretary and general of Alexander the Great. Much about Eumenes’ history is a mystery, which is why Hitoshi Iwaaki took creative liberty to tell his version of his story. While Alexander is famous for being one of the greatest military commanders in history, Eumenes’ name is somewhat forgotten by the world.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Has a Bigger Challenge Than Bringing the X-Men Into the MCU
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Looking back, it seems like the most obvious thing in the world. After decades of successfully intertwining an entire universe of characters in Marvel Comics, it makes complete sense to at least try and bring that same scope and connective tissue to the big screen. But in 2008, Marvel Studios took a huge swing with […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Looking back, it seems like the most obvious thing in the world. After decades of successfully intertwining an entire universe of characters in Marvel Comics, it makes complete sense to at least try and bring that same scope and connective tissue to the big screen. But in 2008, Marvel Studios took a huge swing with Iron Man ’s post-credits scene . If it wasn’t well-received, then Marvel could have simply shrugged it off as a fun reference for hardcore fans. Instead, of course, Nick Fury’s mention of “the Avenger Initiative” gave birth to the Marvel Cinematic Universe and officially set the course for 2012’s The Avengers .

Bringing together Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, and The Hulk — all of whom previously led MCU films — into a crossover team film felt like a magic trick. And the fact that writer-director Joss Whedon effortlessly brought together these characters and their specific corners of the MCU undoubtedly lay the foundation that everything else is built on. Even more remarkably, the MCU has never stopped upping the ante. Throughout both the Infinity Saga and the Multiverse Saga, Marvel Studios has continually taken risks, but the biggest challenge in Avengers: Doomsday isn’t the one most people think it is.

The Avengers had to integrate heroes who, until that point, had occupied separate stories, each with its own unique genre and tone. However, Avengers: Doomsday has an exponentially more difficult task: combining several different teams . In hindsight, much of the Multiverse Saga seemed devoted to sprinkling in breadcrumbs that would gradually assemble a collection of superhero teams. Of course, Fantastic Four: First Steps and Thunderbolts* introduced fans to the Fantastic Four and the New Avengers , respectively. The latter team drew upon several different projects to bring its members into the MCU, especially Black Widow . And the Wakandans are already well established, most notably with Black Panther: Wakanda Forever .

But the past few years of Marvel projects have also been teasing the existence of at least two more teams. Avengers: Doomsday will finally see the MCU come face to face with Fox’s X-Men. Films like Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and The Marvels featured cameos by popular X-Men characters , and Deadpool & Wolverine completed the mutants’ introduction. Meanwhile, X-Men ‘97 — while set in a different universe — reminded fans why they love these characters. But with more than two decades of films , the X-Men, their dynamic, and their powers hardly need an introduction to audiences. Rather, another team will have an uphill battle ahead in Avengers: Doomsday .

The last time the Avengers assembled was at the Battle of Earth. Following Tony Stark’s sacrifice, the team essentially disbanded. From a creative standpoint, this made sense for the MCU, as it would give the Multiverse Saga space to rebuild Earth’s Mightiest Heroes from the ground up. The trouble was that the Avengers still haven’t been rebuilt at all. In fact, the first mention of reassembling them was in Captain America: Brave New World , released just a year before Avengers: Doomsday . And yet, the new Avengers led by Sam Wilson’s Captain America — not the New Avengers led, it seems, by Florence Pugh’s Yelena Belova — will be central to this climactic chapter. In addition to Captain America, the team will reportedly include Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Shang-Chi (Simu Liu), and Falcon (Danny Ramirez).

If this were a less complicated Avengers sequel, that team wouldn’t feel so rushed. But as Thor points out in the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer, he doesn’t even know who half of the heroes in the film are. With the exception of his relationship with Falcon, we don’t even know what Captain America’s leadership looks like. And this Avengers team is the only team in the film that doesn’t have even a single movie where they work together. It’s hard to imagine Avengers: Doomsday will have much of a chance to establish this new team dynamic before they rush into action due to all the whole universes colliding. With so much of a focus on expanding its hero roster, the Multiverse Saga forgot to connect all the dots within the Sacred Timeline , which would have only raised the stakes when other teams enter the fight.

Do you think the Multiverse Saga should have laid more groundwork to establish Captain America’s new Avengers team? Let us know in the comments section below!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

articles.title: ‘Outlander: Blood of My Blood' Bosses on the Season 2 Finale Twist That Would Rewrite the Series' Lore, Who Won't Appear on the Show — and Its Uncertain Future
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers from “Twelfth Night,” the Season 2 finale of “Outlander: Blood of My Blood,” now streaming on Starz. “Outlander” was never a series to hold back on a brainy twist that took a minute to digest. But its prequel series, “Outlander: Blood of My Blood,” may have outdone its predecessor […]
articles.content:
SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers from “Twelfth Night,” the Season 2 finale of “ Outlander: Blood of My Blood ,” now streaming on Starz.

“Outlander” was never a series to hold back on a brainy twist that took a minute to digest. But its prequel series, “Outlander: Blood of My Blood,” may have outdone its predecessor with a twist that rewrites at least one family tree.

Since the prequel premiered last year, it has always operated on its own narrative timeline, separate from author Diana Gabaldon’s book series. In those books, Julia (Hermoine Corfield) and Henry (Jeremy Irvine), the parents of original series heroine Claire (Caitriona Balfe), died when she was 5 years old in a car crash. But with “Blood of My Blood,” executive producers Matthew B. Roberts and Maril Davis ponder what might have happened if they actually time-traveled through the same magic stones their daughter would decades later, and were left to survive in 1710s Scotland.

It has been one tragedy after another for the lovebirds, and that’s saying something, given that they weathered World War I. But one question has loomed large over the Beauchamps: What will happen to their son, William, with whom Julia was pregnant when they went through the stones? He’s not in Gabaldon’s books, so Roberts and Davis have a bit of freedom to play with his fate. And they seemingly gave fans their answer in the Season 2 finale.

Julia and Henry were dealt their biggest setback yet earlier this season, when a seer informed her she isn’t a time traveler, she was just pregnant with one. William has his father’s mystical gene, and now that Julia is postpartum, she won’t be able to go back to her own time unless they get pregnant again, which itself is a moral quandary. The news doesn’t stop them from trying to run away together again. But in the process, Henry is shot by Lord Lovat (Tony Curran) in a case of mistaken identity, and Julia’s attempts to flee Lovat’s henchman leave her lifeless at the bottom of a waterfall. Fearful for wee William’s life without his parents, Julia’s confidante Davina (Sarah Vickers) takes him to the safest place she can think of –– to her son Brian (Jamie Roy) and his new wife Ellen (Harriet Slater). Mere moments after Brian and Ellen’s long-awaited wedding, the Frasers have a new addition to their future home at Lallybroch. Related Stories Jennifer Lopez on the ‘JLo Show’ Concert Film, Her ‘Happy Era’ and Moving on From Divorce: 'What I Thought Love Was Really Isn’t Love’ ‘Morning Show’ Star Mark Duplass and Katie Aselton Show Off Their Three Rescue Dogs in PETA Ad (EXCLUSIVE)

This is where the series goes for broke, and makes a frankly brazen claim. Brian and Ellen are, of course, the parents of future “Outlander” hero Jamie (Sam Heughan). According to Gabaldon’s original books, he had an older brother named William (aka Willie), whose death when Jamie was young forever affected how he saw the world and cared for those he loved. (Not for nothing, Willie was so formative for Jamie that fans latched onto the wooden snake he carved before he died, and the onscreen prop sold for more than $5,000 at auction earlier this year.)
